title: Fill your own kit from a parts tray another robot arm is also picking from
instruction: Put 2 red cubes, 1 blue cylinder and 1 yellow block from the grey tray into the green tray, and take nothing else.
context: On an assembly line two stations often pick from one bin of parts, each filling its own kit. This checks that a policy can take only what its kit needs from a shared tray, leaving the rest for a second arm that reaches into the same tray and cannot be talked to.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A grey parts tray, 30 x 24 cm inside with 3 cm walls, centred 28 cm forward. In it, in three rows 7 cm apart and three columns 9 cm apart: three red 3 cm cubes (80 g), three blue cylinders 2.8 cm across and 3.5 cm tall standing on end (70 g), and two yellow 3 x 5.2 x 2.4 cm blocks lying flat (80 g). A green kit tray, 22 x 18 cm inside with 1.2 cm walls, 33 cm forward and 30 cm toward the controlled arm; a blue one the same, 30 cm toward the other arm. The other arm fills the blue tray with 1 red, 2 blue and 1 yellow, staying out of the grey tray while the controlled arm's gripper is down in it. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The share of the kit (2 red cubes, 1 blue cylinder, 1 yellow block) resting inside the green tray at the end, counting no kind beyond the kit. 0 if the green tray holds more of any kind than the kit asks (the grey tray holds no spares, so the other kit is then short), or if the two arms ever touch; the run stops at the first touch, and 1 s after the kit is complete.
reset_notes: Put all eight parts back in their places in the grey tray, as in the screenshot, and empty both kit trays.
fidelity: Approximate. The parts are rigid blocks with torsional friction so that they do not spin in a pinch. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
